title: Durable preflight reasons clear 'on the next snapshot or event', but forge CLI status and folder trust have neither
evidence: 03c-goals.md:117-121 (machine marked unfit for PUSH_ACCESS_MISSING, FOLDER_UNTRUSTED etc. 'until the next snapshot or event changes the fact'); snapshot.proto:361 and :263-278 (ForgeCliStatus and RepoAccess exist only in Snapshot.forge_cli); events.proto:40-102 (no forge-status or trust event); 01-agent-capabilities.md:97 and :376-378 (H4 is kind S only, cached 1 h); 03c-goals.md:64-65 (planning rule 3 reads ForgeCliStatus.signed_in and push_access); snapshot.proto:82-108 (HarnessInfo carries no folder-trust fact).
problem: Snapshots are sent only on connect or SnapshotRequest, and a healthy agent can stay connected for weeks. After the owner runs `gh auth login` or fixes repo access, the hub's copy stays stale and the machine remains unfit for that harness/repo. FOLDER_UNTRUSTED has no observable fact at all on the wire. The same stale copy also lets the hub plan onto a machine whose gh token has expired, wasting a dispatch.
fix: Either add an additive Event.forge_cli_status (COALESCE per host) sent when the agent's hourly H4 re-check changes, or add a hub rule that re-runs Preflight or SnapshotRequest for durable-unfit machines at a fixed interval. The re-check rule also covers FOLDER_UNTRUSTED, which has no event. Fix the 03c:120 wording to match whichever is chosen.
verify: Confirmed. ForgeCliStatus/RepoAccess exist only in Snapshot.forge_cli (snapshot.proto:263-278, :361); the Event body oneof (events.proto:40-102) has no forge-status or folder-trust event, and H4 is kind S only (01-agent-capabilities.md:97). 03c-goals.md:117-121 (and command_goal.proto:102-103) mark a machine unfit for durable reasons 'until the next snapshot or event changes the fact', but snapshots are sent only on connect or SnapshotRequest, and nothing in the docs triggers a re-check for a durable-unfit machine (grep of SnapshotRequest reasons shows only event_gap and slot_mismatch). FOLDER_UNTRUSTED has no observable fact anywhere on the wire. Recovery after `gh auth login` therefore depends on a reconnect or an operator retry, which undercuts the 'minimal owner attention' goal.
resolution: events.proto: new Event.forge_cli_status (54, COALESCE "forge:<tool>:<host>") sent when the hourly H4 re-check changes; hub re-runs Preflight for durably unfit (machine, harness, repo) after 10 min doubling to 1 h (this is how FOLDER_UNTRUSTED clears) and treats a ForgeCliStatus older than 2 h as unknown. 02i "Durable facts", 03c:138-145, 01 H4.

title: The event delivery table covers 16 of 28 body kinds, and sequence gaps are ambiguous
evidence: events.proto:4-8 and :33-35 (class 'fixed per kind in 02-contracts.md'); 02-contracts.md:247-258 (the backpressure table lists pane_summary, resource_sample, spool_status, usage_reading, branch_state, probe_health, activity, prompt_detected/gone, harness_condition, local_approval, availability, goal_state, pane_exited, power_state, drain_state); events.proto:40-102 (unlisted bodies: account_identity, harness_changed, session_account_link, tmux_server, session, window, pane_created, harness_ready, harness_hook, pane_harness_session, repo, policy_changed); 02-contracts.md:212-214 (ring 'latest state per pane wins'); 02-contracts.md:256-257 (Heartbeat.event_seq reveals a gap that a SnapshotRequest repairs).
problem: The agent sets Event.delivery and coalesce_key from this table, so twelve kinds, including the inventory events and harness_hook, have no defined class or coalesce key, and the ring's collapse rule is only stated for per-pane state. Because seq is assigned agent-wide and shed or coalesced events leave gaps, the hub cannot tell an expected SHED gap from a lost event, so a naive hub gap check would fire SnapshotRequest continuously under normal pane-summary shedding.
fix: Complete the table with a class and coalesce_key for every body kind. State the ring collapse rule per class and whether shed or coalesced events consume a seq. State that only a gap in NEVER_DROP kinds, or ring overflow, triggers SnapshotRequest.
verify: Confirmed. The table at 02-contracts.md:247-258 omits account_identity, harness_changed, session_account_link, tmux_server, session, window, pane_created, harness_ready, harness_hook, pane_harness_session, repo and policy_changed, although events.proto:4-8 and :33-35 say the class is fixed per kind there and the agent stamps Event.delivery and coalesce_key from it. 02-contracts.md:256-257 also says a shedding gap in Heartbeat.event_seq is visible and a SnapshotRequest repairs it, which conflicts with 03-workflows.md:255-262 (gap from ring overflow), leaving it unstated whether shed events consume seq numbers. Doc-only fix, low risk.
resolution: New docs/specs/02i-delivery-and-sequencing.md holds the class and coalesce_key of every Event body (31 kinds) plus the queue/ring rule per class and states that every event consumes a seq; events.proto body comments name each class, and 02-contracts.md points to 02i instead of its short table.

title: AWAITING_LOCAL_CONFIRM is an 'interim CommandResult', contradicting 'exactly one CommandResult' and ResultAck
evidence: status.proto:64-65 (STATUS_AWAITING_LOCAL_CONFIRM); 02-contracts.md:171 ('exactly one CommandResult') and :328 ('interim; a final result follows'); 02-contracts.md:157 (L3 carried as Status in CommandResult); agent.proto:258-261 (ResultAck lets the agent forget a result); command.proto:92-110 (CommandProgress already has status, reason and message); events.proto:252-261.
problem: If the interim state is a CommandResult, the hub's ResultAck, outbox transition to done and the agent's 'known command_id returns its logged result' rule would treat it as final, and the later real result would be a second result for the same command_id. The pending deadline and who must approve are not carried.
fix: Carry the interim state as CommandProgress{step:'awaiting_local_confirm', status: AWAITING_LOCAL_CONFIRM} with the deadline in metadata. Keep CommandResult single and terminal, and mark AWAITING_LOCAL_CONFIRM as progress-only in the status pairing table and in 02-contracts.md:157.
verify: Confirmed contradiction. 02-contracts.md:171 says the agent sends exactly one CommandResult, and 02-contracts.md:157 (L3) and :328 carry AWAITING_LOCAL_CONFIRM as an interim Status 'in CommandResult' with a final result to follow. status.proto:64-65 defines it as a Status value. ResultAck (agent.proto:258-261) lets the agent forget results, so treating the interim as a result is ambiguous. CommandProgress (command.proto:92-110) already carries status, reason, message and metadata and is the natural carrier. The fix is small and additive.
resolution: AWAITING_LOCAL_CONFIRM is now progress only: CommandProgress{step "awaiting_local_confirm", step_index 0, deadline in metadata}; CommandResult stays single and final. Fixed in status.proto, command.proto, 02-contracts (L3 row, error table, envelope checks), 02g, 02h and 01c.

title: Agent event seq and hub connection epoch can regress after a crash or restore, silently discarding events or commands
evidence: events.proto:27-28 says seq is 'persisted, never reused'; W2 persists only the ring ('per event, fsync batched <= 1 s', 03-workflows.md:299) and the ring holds only never-dropped/coalesced kinds (03-workflows.md:254-255), so SHED events (pane_summary, resource_sample, heartbeat-adjacent) consume seq numbers that are never persisted. The hub applies later events 'only if seq > last_event_seq' (03-workflows.md:173-175) and keeps hub_last_event_seq per machine (agent.proto:178-179). After an agent crash the counter restarts from the last persisted ring seq and re-emits numbers the hub already saw, which are dropped as duplicates; same after a state-dir wipe or VM revert (install_id changes, seq restarts at 1). On the hub side the epoch is 'epoch+1' of the stored value (03-workflows.md:248); after a store restore (03-workflows.md:325) the hub can issue an epoch the agent already used (Hello.last_epoch=7, last_applied_command_seq=41, agent.proto:154-155), and the agent then rejects the new epoch's seq 1..41 as SEQ_REPLAYED (02-contracts.md envelope checks).
problem: No rule keeps either counter monotonic across crash/restore, and nothing tells the hub that an agent's seq space was reset.
fix: Specify: the agent persists a seq high-water mark in reserved blocks and sets its floor to max(local, HelloAck.hub_last_event_seq) after each HelloAck. The hub sets epoch = max(stored, Hello.last_epoch) + 1 and treats Hello.last_event_seq < hub_last_event_seq as agent rollback (keep history, SnapshotRequest{reason='seq_rollback'}). Add seq high-water mark and install_id to the agent state-dir lists and a row to the W2 failure table.
verify: Confirmed no rule keeps either counter monotonic. events.proto:27 says seq is 'persisted, never reused', but the persisted ring (03-workflows.md:299, 254-255) holds only never-dropped and coalesced kinds. Shed events (02-contracts.md:256-258 table: pane_summary, resource_sample, spool_status) consume seq numbers and are never persisted, so after an agent crash the counter restarts from the last ring seq. The hub applies later events 'only if seq > last_event_seq' (03-workflows.md:173-175) and would drop a restarted agent's events as duplicates until it passes the old number; state-dir wipe or VM revert is the same. A repo-wide grep finds no high-water mark, floor or rollback rule. Epoch is 'epoch+1' (03-workflows.md:248) with no max against Hello.last_epoch (agent.proto:154-155), so a restored hub store can reissue an epoch and trip SEQ_REPLAYED (02-contracts.md:183-184). This is a rules gap with no required proto change.
resolution: 02i "Sequence numbers" and "Connection epoch": agent persists seq_hwm in blocks of 1024, floors seq above HelloAck.hub_last_event_seq, hub treats Hello.last_event_seq below its stored value, a counter decrease or a new install_id as agent rollback (event_generation, marker, audit machine.install_changed), epoch = max(stored, Hello.last_epoch)+1 and the agent refuses a regressed epoch. agent.proto comments; W1/W2 persistence and failure rows; 03f restore.

title: Seq-gap detection cannot tell shedding from loss, and 'replayed seq <= Snapshot.seq is history only' contradicts the W2 failure rows
evidence: 03-workflows.md:260-262 and 02-contracts.md:256-258 say Heartbeat.event_seq lets the hub detect a gap 'caused by ring overflow' and by shedding, then repair it with SnapshotRequest{event_gap}. But gaps in seq are normal: SHED events (pane_summary every 5 s per pane, resource_sample, spool_status) and COALESCE replacements (usage, branch_state, probe_health; 03-workflows.md:254-255 'latest per key wins') delete seq numbers by design, so every hub that sees a hole would request a snapshot, and a real loss of a never-dropped event looks identical. Separately, 03-workflows.md:243/:258-260, 02-contracts.md:217 and 03f-hub-internals.md:60 say replayed events with seq <= Snapshot.seq go to history only, yet 03-workflows.md:328 says the replayed PaneExited lets 'W6 evaluate the one-nudge rule once' and :331 says the replayed AvailabilityChanged{keystroke} drives human_at_keyboard_until 'from the replayed timestamp'; :329-330 say HarnessCondition and Prompt events 'raise and retire in one batch'. History-only means none of that runs.
problem: No wire field distinguishes deliberate drops from lost never-drop events, and the apply rule for replayed never-drop events that feed derived goal/triage flags is contradictory.
fix: Doc fix: state that gap detection compares Heartbeat.event_seq with the hub's highest stored seq, never contiguity. Fix the :331 row once last_input_at exists on TmuxPane (snapshot-derived rather than replay-derived). Optionally add a persisted ring_evicted_never_drop_total to Hello/Heartbeat so the timeline gap marker has a wire source.
verify: Partly confirmed, overstated. Real: 03-workflows.md:331 says a replayed AvailabilityChanged{keystroke} drives human_at_keyboard_until 'from the replayed timestamp', while 03-workflows.md:243/:258-260, 02-contracts.md:217 and 03f-hub-internals.md:60 say replayed events with seq <= Snapshot.seq go to history only; the snapshot carries no input timestamp (see goal-pane-input finding), so that row cannot work as written. Also 02-contracts.md:256-258 says Heartbeat.event_seq makes a gap 'caused by shedding' visible and repairable by SnapshotRequest, without saying whether the hub compares highest-seq (stable) or contiguity (would false-trigger). Overstated: the hub compares Heartbeat.event_seq with its highest stored seq, not hole-by-hole, so shed events do not by themselves force a snapshot per hole. The PaneExited row (:328) is consistent with history-only because the snapshot already shows the pane dead. 03-workflows.md failure table already says 'dropped ring entries counted and gap shown on the timeline', though no wire field carries that count.
resolution: New EventCounters{shed_total, coalesced_total, evicted_total} in Hello.event_counters and Heartbeat.events: only a rise of evicted_total is loss (SnapshotRequest event_lost plus a timeline gap marker); contiguity and Heartbeat.event_seq are never used to infer loss. Replay rule rewritten in 02i, 02-contracts and W2: seq <= Snapshot.seq is history only and runs no rule, with a table of the snapshot field that carries each effect; audit rows stay idempotent.

title: SessionLog hole/duplicate handling has no negative ack, gap_before offset semantics are undefined, and a restored hub wedges streams
evidence: 03d-triage-sessions-logs.md:262 accepts a chunk only at the stored end, 'duplicate (re-ack)', and for a hole 'refuse (ack stays)' (:337 'the agent resends from there'). LogAck (streams.proto:143-155) is only sent on success, so after a refusal the agent receives nothing and cannot learn the hub's stored end. gap_before (streams.proto:124) says 'bytes lost before this chunk' but not whether offset skips them; W9 :321 says 'contiguous except across an explicit gap_before' while the accept rule is 'offset = stored end'. Hub restore from an older backup (or 'truncate trailing partial frame to last indexed offset', :326) leaves the hub end below an agent that already dropped spool <= its older ack (:313 'drop spool <= acked_offset'): every later chunk is a hole, the agent no longer has the bytes to resend, and no rule lets it declare a gap. Also 03d:260 and :277-283 still describe one frame per 10 s / 256 KiB, contradicting the S2 framing in streams.proto:105-112 and 02-contracts.md log framing (one frame up to 5 min/4 MiB, frame_start/frame_raw_offset not in the W9 sequence), and the hub writes '<session>/<stream>/<day>.zst' (:263) without saying a day rollover mid-frame must wait for the next frame_start, which replay-from-frame_raw_offset needs.
problem: Missing: hub reply on refused chunks, precise offset arithmetic across gaps, agent behaviour when the hub is behind the agent's spool floor, file-rotation rule for frames, and W9 text/sequence not updated for the frame model.
fix: Hub answers every chunk with LogAck{key, acked_offset = stored_end}, accepted or refused. On acked_offset below its spool floor the agent sends the next chunk with gap_before = floor - acked_offset, offset = floor, frame_start = true. Accept rule becomes offset == stored_end + gap_before. Hub rotates day files only at a frame_start chunk. Rewrite the W9 sequence and rules to the frame model and add frame_start/frame_raw_offset to the log_segments index columns.
verify: Confirmed. 03d-triage-sessions-logs.md:262 accepts a chunk only at the stored end and for a hole 'refuse (ack stays)' (:337 'the agent resends from there'), but LogAck (streams.proto:143-155) is only specified as a success reply, so a refused chunk gives the agent no way to learn the hub's stored end. gap_before (streams.proto:124) does not say whether offset skips the lost bytes, and the 03d accept rule 'offset = stored end' (:262, :321) conflicts with 'contiguous except across an explicit gap_before'. If the hub is restored from backup or truncates (:326) below an agent that already dropped spool <= acked_offset (:313), every later chunk is a hole and the agent cannot resend or declare a gap. 03d:260 and :277-283 still describe zstd frames per 10 s or 256 KiB, contradicting the frame model in streams.proto:105-112 (one frame up to 5 min or 4 MiB, frame_start, frame_raw_offset); the sequence diagram omits both fields. Day-file rotation (:263) is not tied to frame_start, which replay from frame_raw_offset needs.
resolution: streams.proto: LogAck now answers every chunk with acked_offset = stored end and a new LogAckStatus (STORED, DUPLICATE, HOLE, UNKNOWN_STREAM); gap_before semantics defined (offset = acked end + gap_before, accept rule offset == stored_end + gap_before); an agent whose spool floor is above the hub's end sends gap_before = floor - end with frame_start. 03d W9 rewritten to the frame model (day files rotate only at frame_start; frame_start and frame_raw_offset in log_segments), 03f keys.

title: SetLogCapture cannot give the agent a SessionId, so LogStreamKey.session_id is empty for developer sessions
evidence: command_goal.proto:212-215 SetLogCapture{SessionTarget session, enabled}: the target is by tmux_id/name, no hub SessionId. snapshot.proto:159-160 says TmuxSession.session_id is 'empty for the developer's own'. hub session.proto:71-76 says the hub assigns a SessionId to every observed session bound to (machine, server_start_id, tmux_id), and SetLogCaptureRequest carries it (session.proto:260-264). The agent must still fill LogStreamKey{session_id, pane, stream} on every LogChunk (streams.proto:113-131, harness.proto:231-235), name its spool directory spool/<session>/<stream>/ (03d-triage-sessions-logs.md:313) and the hub names files and log_segments by <session> (03d:263, :315).
problem: For the developer-session capture path the agent has no session id to put in the key, so the hub must guess by PaneKey and the spool, ack and replay keys diverge; an empty key.session_id also collides with LogAck.all_streams semantics.
fix: Either document that for developer sessions the agent leaves key.session_id empty, keys its spool by PaneKey, and the hub fills in the SessionId from key.pane, or add an optional SetLogCapture.session_id so the agent echoes it in every LogChunk.key. Pick one and state it in 02-contracts.md K1 and 03d.
verify: Gap confirmed but severity overstated. SetLogCapture (command_goal.proto:212-215) carries a SessionTarget, whose oneof (command_tmux.proto:22-33) holds session_id, name or tmux_id; for a developer session the agent only knows tmux_id (TmuxSession.session_id is empty for developer sessions, snapshot.proto:159-160), so it has no hub SessionId for LogStreamKey.session_id (streams.proto:113-131) or the spool path (03d:313). However PaneKey (ids.proto:91-101) plus the hub's (machine, server_start_id, tmux_id) binding (session.proto:71-76) lets the hub resolve the SessionId from key.pane deterministically, so this is an unstated convention, not an unsolvable problem. The claimed collision with LogAck.all_streams is unfounded (that uses an explicit bool, streams.proto:153-155).
resolution: harness.proto LogStreamKey: on the agent wire the identity is (pane, stream) and session_id is optional, filled in by the hub from (machine, server_start_id, tmux id); LogAck echoes the key as sent; the spool is keyed by pane. SetLogCapture comment, 02-contracts K1 and 03d W9 "Stream identity".

title: Settings rejection and policy safe mode have no wire fields although W10 says the UI shows them
evidence: 03e-settings-and-drift.md:116: an invalid setting is 'named in capped_fields with SettingSource.layer=LOCAL_CEILING and a message; the UI shows the rejection'. SettingsAck (agent.proto:249-256) has only capped_fields as repeated string, no message, no layer, no way to tell 'capped by ceiling' from 'rejected as invalid'; SettingSource (settings.proto:76-80) has no message. 03e:117: policy file invalid -> safe mode, 'PolicyInfo.schema_version="" + message in the snapshot; triage policy_invalid'; PolicyInfo (snapshot.proto:297-303) has schema_version, hash, loaded_at, changed_since_load only: no safe_mode flag, no error text, and an empty schema_version is an implicit sentinel. Safe-mode rejections of every control command have no distinct reason (status.proto only has POLICY_DENIED=13 in the preflight range, 02-contracts.md:314 table).
problem: The hub cannot raise policy_invalid or show why a setting was not applied; telemetry fleet_agent_policy_safe_mode and fleet_hub_settings_rejected_fields_total (03e:129-133) have no source on the wire.
fix: Additive: PolicyInfo.safe_mode and PolicyInfo.error (short, no file contents); SettingsAck.rejected_fields[] {field, reason, message} kept apart from capped_fields; an envelope-range reason code for safe-mode rejections. Update 03e:116-117.
verify: Confirmed. 03e-settings-and-drift.md:116 says an invalid setting is named in capped_fields 'with SettingSource.layer=LOCAL_CEILING and a message', but SettingsAck (agent.proto:249-256) has only repeated string capped_fields and SettingSource (settings.proto:76-80) has only field and layer, so nothing carries the message or distinguishes 'capped' from 'rejected as invalid'. 03e:117 says safe mode reports 'PolicyInfo.schema_version="" + message', but PolicyInfo (snapshot.proto:297-303) has no message or safe_mode field and the empty-string sentinel is implicit; a repo-wide grep for safe_mode/policy_invalid finds only 03e. The telemetry in 03e:129-133 has no wire source. Low risk, additive.
resolution: agent.proto SettingsAck.rejected[] of the new type/v1 SettingRejection{field, reason, message}, kept apart from capped_fields; snapshot.proto PolicyInfo.safe_mode and error; status.proto REASON_CODE_POLICY_SAFE_MODE (208, REJECTED_BY_POLICY); hub machine.proto rejected_settings, policy_safe_mode, policy_error. 03e rows, 02g audit row, 02-contracts error table.

title: LogStreamKey requires a hub-assigned SessionId the agent cannot know for developer sessions
evidence: api/fleet/type/v1/harness.proto:231-235 LogStreamKey{session_id, pane, stream} is the key of every LogChunk (api/fleet/agent/v1/streams.proto:131 key = 12) and LogAck (:151). api/fleet/agent/v1/snapshot.proto:159-160 TmuxSession.session_id is `empty for the developer's own`. api/fleet/hub/v1/session.proto:68-72 says the hub assigns a SessionId to developer sessions, bound to (machine, server_start_id, tmux_id). api/fleet/agent/v1/command_goal.proto:212-215 SetLogCapture addresses the session by SessionTarget, whose `by` is a oneof of session_id OR name OR tmux_id (command_tmux.proto:22-35), so one command cannot carry both the tmux id and the hub SessionId. docs/specs/02-contracts.md:152,263 and 03d-triage-sessions-logs.md:274-286 define the stream as `LogStreamKey{session_id, pane, stream}` and say LogAck must name exactly the chunk's stream.
problem: K1 lets the owner turn on capture for a developer's own session, but the agent has no value to put in LogStreamKey.session_id and no message through which the hub tells it one. The hub's log index (03f-hub-internals.md:110, `log_segments(session_id, stream, raw_offset)`) is keyed by that session id. Either the agent sends an empty session_id and the hub invents the mapping silently, or there is a missing assignment message.
fix: Simplest option is A. PaneKey (server, server_start_id, pane_id) is already unique per machine, and the hub knows the machine from the certificate. So the agent-wire stream identity is (pane, stream), and LogStreamKey.session_id is optional on agent->hub (agent sets it only when it has FLEET_SESSION_ID). The hub resolves the pane to a SessionId on ingest, and LogAck echoes the key as sent. Document this in the LogStreamKey comment and in 02-contracts.md K1.
verify: Confirmed. harness.proto:231-235 LogStreamKey{session_id, pane, stream}. snapshot.proto:159-160 TmuxSession.session_id is empty for the developer's own. session.proto:68-72 has the hub assign a SessionId bound to (machine, server_start_id, tmux_id). command_goal.proto:212-215 SetLogCapture carries a SessionTarget oneof (session_id OR tmux_id), so the hub cannot hand the agent its assigned id there. No other hub-to-agent message carries the assignment. 03d:261 and 02-contracts.md:152 still show session_id in the key.
resolution: Same change as dev-session-log-key (option A): LogStreamKey.session_id is optional on the agent wire, the hub resolves the pane to its SessionId on ingest; documented in harness.proto, 02-contracts K1 and 03d.

title: An older agent silently ignores new tighten-only settings, and probe-interval merge and precedence are undefined
evidence: type/v1/settings.proto:46-73 (SettingValues grows by adding fields; 'unset = no opinion'); agent/v1/agent.proto:232-256 (Settings and SettingsAck.effective, capped_fields only for the local ceiling); docs/specs/02-contracts.md:299 (one capability `settings`, no per-field versioning); docs/specs/02-contracts.md:283-287 (hub supports agents one minor version behind); docs/specs/03e-settings-and-drift.md:36-50 (merge rules list does not include `probe_interval` or `merged_grace`). Probe interval has three carriers: type/v1/settings.proto:69-70, agent/v1/agent.proto:243-245 (`probe_interval_by_account`, 'tighten-only'), agent/v1/command_tmux.proto:48 (EnsureProbe.interval).
problem: A hub upgraded first can send a safety setting (for example a new limit or `block_on_battery`-style flag) that an older agent drops as an unknown field. The ack's `effective` simply omits it, which the UI cannot tell apart from 'no opinion', so the owner believes it is enforced. For probe intervals, 'tighter' is ambiguous (a local floor on frequency is a max, not min(hub, local)) and which of the three channels wins on conflict is unstated. `merged_grace` is hub-only but is delivered to agents.
fix: Add `SettingsAck.unrecognized_fields` (or a `settings_schema` integer in Hello/SettingsAck) so the hub can mark 'not enforced on this agent'. Alternatively advertise `settings.<field>` capabilities. Write the probe-interval merge rule (local value is a minimum interval) and a precedence order (Settings.probe_interval_by_account, then SettingValues.probe_interval, with EnsureProbe.interval only run_now or initial). Remove hub-only fields from agent delivery or mark them echo-only. Additive.
verify: critic (verified in files by the critic)
resolution: SettingsAck.unrecognized_value_fields and unrecognized_settings_fields (field numbers) let the hub show "not enforced on this machine" (hub Machine.status.unenforced_settings) and keep the machine out of auto-dispatch for a safety limit. Probe interval: precedence by-account > SettingValues.probe_interval > EnsureProbe.interval (initial only), effective = max(hub, local minimum), reported in EffectiveSettings.probe_interval_by_account; merged_grace marked hub-only echo. 03e, settings protos.

title: Agent-clock timestamps drive ordering and waits with only a 5-minute warning for skew
evidence: agent/v1/events.proto:28-30 (`Event.at` agent clock), agent/v1/usage.proto:28-29 (`UsageReading.read_at`), agent/v1/screen.proto:61-64 (resets_at resolved by the agent); hub/v1/machine.proto:151-152 (clock_skew, warning above 5 min); docs/specs/03b-usage-and-sync.md:57,143-144,167 (newest `read_at` wins across machines; ordered by read_at); docs/specs/02-contracts.md:195-197 says skew is measured from `Heartbeat.sent_at` while docs/specs/03-workflows.md:192 says `Hello.sent_at`.
problem: On probe failover two machines read the same account. Newest `read_at` wins, so a machine whose clock is a few minutes fast makes an older reading look current, and `reading_stale` (read_at vs previous reset) is skew-sensitive. A badly wrong or future `Event.at` is stored with no clamp. The contract never says the hub records its own receive time, and the skew source is inconsistent between docs.
fix: State in 02-contracts: the hub stores `received_at` for every event and reading, orders cross-machine data by hub-adjusted time (`at - machine.clock_skew`) or received_at, clamps `at` beyond now plus skew to received_at, and uses one skew source (Hello.sent_at at connect, Heartbeat.sent_at thereafter). Add `received_time` to the hub UsageReading. Additive.
verify: critic (verified in files by the critic)
resolution: Hub is the time authority (02i "Clocks"): received_time on everything, one skew source (Hello.sent_time then Heartbeat.sent_time, median of 5), hub-adjusted time clamped to received_time for future stamps, cross-machine ordering by adjusted read_time with received_time tie-break, clock_untrusted above 15 min. hub UsageReading gains received_time and agent_read_time; MachineTelemetry.clock_untrusted; 02-contracts, W1 and 03b aligned.
